arxiv-2112-09942.title: Influence of external field direction on polarization rotation in antiferroelectric squaric acid H 2 C 4 O 4
arxiv-2112-09942.creator: A. P. Moina
arxiv-2112-09942.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by A. P. Moina. Using the previously developed model we explore the processes of polarization rotation in antiferroelectric crystals of squaric acid by the electric fields directed arbitrarily within the a ​ c ac plane. Except for some particular directions of the field, the two-step polarization reorientation at low temperatures is predicted: first, to the noncollinear phase with perpendicular sublattice polarizations and then to the collinear ferroelectric phase.

arxiv-2202-08325.title: A Data-Augmentation Is Worth A Thousand Samples: Exact Quantification From Analytical Augmented Sample Moments
arxiv-2202-08325.creator: Randall Balestriero, Ishan Misra, Yann LeCun
arxiv-2202-08325.description: Abstract Data-Augmentation (DA) is known to improve performance across tasks and datasets. We propose a method to theoretically analyze the effect of DA and study questions such as: how many augmented samples are needed to correctly estimate the information encoded by that DA? How does the augmentation policy impact the final parameters of a model?

arxiv-2209-06100.title: Study of Spherical Array Target for Long-Baseline Neutrino Experiment
arxiv-2209-06100.creator: Quynh M. Nguyen, Alberto Marchionni
arxiv-2209-06100.description: Abstract Spherical Array Target was studied by implementing the geometry in LBNE’s Beam Simulation source code g4lbne version v3r2p4 and Monte Carlo. To compare with Nominal LBNE target, unoscillated Far Detector neutrino flux was produced using different parameters: sphere diameter 17mm and 13mm, different longitudinal positions, two interaction length and less, beam size R/3 and 1.

arxiv-2304-14158.title: Dissipation and the information content of the deviation from hamiltonian dynamics
arxiv-2304-14158.creator: Marius Buliga
arxiv-2304-14158.description: Abstract We explain a dissipative version of hamiltonian mechanics, based on the information content of the deviation from hamiltonian dynamics. From this formulation we deduce minimal dissipation principles, dynamical inclusions, or constrained evolution with hamiltonian drift reformulations. Among applications we recover a dynamics generalization of Mielke et al quasistatic rate-independent processes.

arxiv-2403-15236.title: ACCESS: Assurance Case Centric Engineering of Safety-critical Systems
arxiv-2403-15236.creator: Ran Wei, Simon Foster, Haitao Mei, Fang Yan, Ruizhe Yang, Ibrahim Habli, Colin O’Halloran, Nick Tudor, Tim Kelly, Yakoub Nemouchi
arxiv-2403-15236.description: Abstract Assurance cases are used to communicate and assess confidence in critical system properties such as safety and security. Historically, assurance cases have been manually created documents, which are evaluated by system stakeholders through lengthy and complicated processes. In recent years, model-based system assurance approaches have gained popularity to improve the efficiency and quality of system assurance activities.

arxiv-2409-00980.title: DNN-GDITD: Out-of-distribution detection via Deep Neural Network based Gaussian Descriptor for Imbalanced Tabular Data
arxiv-2409-00980.creator: Priyanka Chudasama, Anil Surisetty, Aakarsh Malhotra, Alok Singh, {priyanka.chudasama, anil.surisetty, aakarsh.malhotra, alok.singh2}@mastercard.com
arxiv-2409-00980.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Priyanka Chudasama, Anil Surisetty, Aakarsh Malhotra, Alok Singh, {priyanka.chudasama, anil.surisetty, aakarsh.malhotra, alok.singh2}@mastercard.com. Classification tasks present challenges due to class imbalances and evolving data distributions. Addressing these issues requires a robust method to handle imbalances while effectively detecting out-of-distribution (OOD) samples not encountered during training. This study introduces a novel OOD detection algorithm designed for tabular datasets, titled D eep N eural N etwork-based G aussian D escriptor for I mbalanced T abular D ata ( DNN-GDITD ).

arxiv-2409-03866.title: Decoherence due to the Casimir effect?
arxiv-2409-03866.creator: Anirudh Gundhi
arxiv-2409-03866.description: Abstract Open system dynamics of an electron is studied in the presence of radiation field, confined between two parallel conducting pates. It has been suggested in previous works that the quantized zero-point modes of this field lead to finite decoherence effects, possibly due to the Casimir force.

arxiv-2504-05521.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning Algorithms for Option Hedging
arxiv-2504-05521.creator: Andrei Neagu, Frédéric Godin, Leila Kosseim
arxiv-2504-05521.description: Abstract Dynamic hedging is a financial strategy that consists in periodically transacting one or multiple financial assets to offset the risk associated with a correlated liability. Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) algorithms have been used to find optimal solutions to dynamic hedging problems by framing them as sequential decision-making problems.

arxiv-2504-17856.title: Naive Gaussian approximation in a quark-meson model
arxiv-2504-17856.creator: György Wolf
arxiv-2504-17856.description: Abstract A sequence of approximations is derived to go beyond the mean-field level in the case of a simple linear sigma model. A naive, local version of the Gaussian approximation is discussed for the 2 + 1 2+1 flavor extended Polyakov quark-meson model at finite temperature and chemical potential.

arxiv-2505-14034.title: Selected open cluster sample for validating atmospheric parameters: Application to Gaia and other surveys
arxiv-2505-14034.creator: Tong Tang(唐通), Songmei Qin(秦松梅), Jing Zhong(钟靖), Yueyue Jiang(蒋悦悦), Li Chen(陈力)
arxiv-2505-14034.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Tong Tang(唐通), Songmei Qin(秦松梅), Jing Zhong(钟靖), Yueyue Jiang(蒋悦悦), Li Chen(陈力). Reliable stellar atmospheric parameters are essential for probing stellar structure and evolution, and for stellar population studies. However, various deviations appear in comparisons with different ground-based spectroscopic surveys.

arxiv-2601-06719.title: FO-Complete Program Verification for Heap Logics DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: Make sure to enter the correct conference title from your rights confirmation emai; June 03–05, 2018; Woodstock, NY Price: 15.00 ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/18/06
arxiv-2601-06719.creator: Adithya Murali, Hrishikesh Balakrishnan, Aaron Councilman, P. Madhusudan
arxiv-2601-06719.description: Abstract . We develop the first two heap logics that have implicit heaplets and that admit FO-complete program verification. The notion of FO-completeness is a theoretical guarantee that all theorems that are valid when recursive definitions are interpreted as fixpoint definitions (instead of least fixpoint) are guaranteed to be eventually proven by the system.

plos-pone-0003117.description: PLOS ONE research article. Endothelial inflammation with chemokine involvement contributes to acute coronary syndromes (ACS). We tested the hypothesis that variation in the chemokine gene CXCL5 , which encodes epithelial neutrophil-activating peptide (ENA-78), is associated with ACS prognosis. We also inve

pmc-10580986.title: A large-scale phylogeny-guided analysis of pseudogenes in Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacterium
pmc-10580986.creator: Nimrod Cohen, Isana Veksler-Lublinsky
pmc-10580986.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Pseudogenes, once considered "junk DNA" based on the incorrect assumption that the absence of full coding potential means a complete lack of functionality, have recently become a subject of significant interest in the scientific community. Concurrently, it is widely assumed that bacterial genomes are compact and have a high density of coding genes with little room for non-coding genes, including pseudogenes.

pmc-11728266.title: Effects of Different Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation Intensities over Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex on Brain Electrical Activity and Heart Rate Variability in Healthy and Fibromyalgia Women: A Randomized Crossover Trial
pmc-11728266.creator: Mari Carmen Gomez-Alvaro, Narcis Gusi, Ricardo Cano-Plasencia, Juan Luis Leon-Llamas, Alvaro Murillo-Garcia, Maria Melo-Alonso, Santos Villafaina, Matteo Ponzano
pmc-11728266.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). People with fibromyalgia (FM) exhibit alterations in brain electrical activity and autonomic modulation compared to healthy individuals. Objectives: This study aimed to investigate transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) effects on brain electrocortical activity and heart rate variability (HRV), specifically targeting the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex in both healthy controls (HC) and FM groups, to identify potential differences in the responses between these groups, and to compare the effectiveness of two distinct tDCS intensities (1 mA and 2 mA) against a sham condition.

pmc-12635109.title: Light-induced current in Cooper pair insulators in NbTiN films
pmc-12635109.creator: Alexey Mironov, Valerii Vinokur
pmc-12635109.description: The usual macroscopic Cooper pairs systems, the superconductors, very weakly interact with the visible light since self-existing superconducting currents screen the light penetration into the samples. However, the superinsulators whose superinsulating behavior is caused by localization of Cooper pairs demonstrate significant interaction with light.

pmc-12655356.title: Distribution of Rotavirus alphagastroenteritidis Strains in Blantyre, Malawi, During and After the COVID-19 Pandemic
pmc-12655356.creator: End Chinyama, Chimwemwe Mhango, Rothwell Taia, Landilani Gauti, Jonathan Mandolo, Flywell Kawonga, Ernest Matambo, Prisca Matambo, Innocent Chibwe, Richard Wachepa, Nigel A. Cunliffe, Chisomo L. Msefula, Khuzwayo C. Jere
pmc-12655356.description: Rotavirus alphagastroenteritidis remains the leading cause of severe gastroenteritis in children under five years, despite widespread vaccine use. The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted healthcare and vaccination delivery, while non-pharmacological interventions may have influenced R. alphagastroenteritidis transmission. We conducted hospital-based surveillance of R. alphagastroenteritidis gastroenteritis at Queen Elizabeth Central Hospital (QECH) in Blantyre, Malawi, from October 2019 to October 2024.

pmc-12673486.title: Potential diagnostic markers and therapeutic targets for obstructive sleep apnea with comorbid depression based on bioinformatics analysis
pmc-12673486.creator: Yinfei Lu, Zao Tang, Xiangyu Zhou, Wanting Lin, Xiao Guo
pmc-12673486.description: BackgroundObstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and major depressive disorder (MDD) impose substantial quality-of-life burdens and socioeconomic costs. Growing evidence indicates bidirectional disease interactions that exacerbate clinical outcomes. This study identifies diagnostic biomarkers and explores therapeutic targets underlying OSA-MDD comorbidity.MethodsWe analyzed OSA/MDD-specific differentially expressed genes (DEGs) from Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) identified co-expressed modules.

pmc-12678832.title: Evaluation of the SLS CHARTER care model to support post-stroke care continuity and employment
pmc-12678832.creator: Estelle Foo Jie Wei, Wan Fen Yip, Joey Ha Wei Yee, Ryan Cheok, Nuez Odessa Setiota, Deshan Kumar, Carol Tham, Lim Pang Hung, Loh Yong Joo, Michelle Jessica Pereira
pmc-12678832.description: The Stroke Life Support Central Health Alliance, Registry & Technology Enabled caRe (SLS CHARTER) Programme addresses stroke patients’ rehabilitation needs through timely evaluation and intervention, but it has not been evaluated. This study evaluated the programme’s outcomes over 6 months. The primary outcome was Post Stroke Checklist (PSC) usage per SLS participant.

pmc-13364350.title: KetoFLEX 12/3 Diet and Cognitive Health: A Precision-Nutrition Perspective on Mechanisms, Emerging Evidence, and Future Directions
pmc-13364350.creator: Rammohan V. Rao, Kaavya G. Subramaniam, Julie Gregory, Aida L. Bredesen, Christine Coward, Sho Okada, Lance Kelly, Dale E. Bredesen
pmc-13364350.description: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disorder characterized by impaired glucose metabolism, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammation, oxidative stress, and progressive cognitive decline. Because currently available pharmacological therapies provide only modest symptomatic benefit, nutrition-based interventions are increasingly being explored as complementary strategies for supporting brain metabolism and cognitive resilience.

pmc-13376384.title: CircRAD23B-208aa Promotes Gastric Cancer Progression by Activating the Unfolded Protein Response through PDIA5 SUMOylation
pmc-13376384.creator: Yuli Chen, Jiahao Guo, Ziwei Li, Shaokun Yu, Xiao Ke, Qinnan Chen, Hao Wu, Ming Sun, Fengqi Nie, Xianghua Liu
pmc-13376384.description: Gastric cancer (GC) remains a lethal malignancy with limited therapeutic options and poor prognosis. In this study, we employed integrated RNA sequencing and ribosome nascent-chain complex sequencing analyses to identify a coding circular RNA (circRNA), circRAD23B, which is markedly up-regulated in GC tissues. Its expression correlates strongly with advanced tumor stage, lymph node metastasis, and reduced overall survival.

pmc-13425514.title: Batch Adsorption Kinetics and Isotherm Modeling of Thiocyanate Using Reduced GO-Metal Oxide Nanocomposites
pmc-13425514.creator: Abdulelah H. Alsulami
pmc-13425514.description: The elimination of thiocyanate (SCN–), a persistent and hazardous pollutant in industrial effluents, constitutes a significant environmental issue. This study presents the synthesis and deployment of a new nanocomposite of reduced graphene oxide functionalized with metal oxides (rGO-Al2O3/MgO/K2O) for effective SCN– adsorption.

pmc-13526875.title: A soft diet attenuates exercise-induced increases in cortical bone density and formation in long bones in growing mice
pmc-13526875.creator: Yasuhiro Shimizu, Fatma Rashed, Huan Cao, Yuki Arai, Takashi Ono, Kazuhiro Aoki
pmc-13526875.description: Bone and muscle are closely linked through functional interdependence. Training and regular exercise can improve and maintain optimal bone mass and strength. Here, we investigated the effects of exercise combined with soft versus hard diet (pellet) on long bones in mice.
